items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Ernie Anderson, who now handles Charles Bronson

ctx.x: I think it is called Comes Jazz. And it is fronted by me, although it had been Condon's group which, I fronted.

A very interesting thing, to get away from Dave Tough Tuft a minute, a lot of people think that the Summa Cum Laude band was my band. Well, of course, it wasn't. I had just left Benny Goodman and I hadn't the faintest idea what I was going to do. I knew I didn't want to be a band leader and Ernie Anderson, who now handles Charles Bronson and he is sort of a genius at publicity, was handling Eddie Condon, and as I say, there was a lot of publicity, Tommy Dorsey and Benny Goodman had this little war on and I got a…

Dave Bowman, a Canadian pianist who was one of the finest I had ever played with; Brad Gowans, the beautiful valve trombone player; Pee Wee Russell, of course, who became a world -- I want to talk about Pee Wee later; Max Kaminsky was still going very strongly; and then Eddie on tuning what Eddie called the pork chop, ukelele guitar; and myself on tenor.
